answer: Reputation-weighted transaction sequencing. Each identity's throughput share is its trailing useful-work score divided by total network score, so honest agents climb and clones start at zero every dawn. A clone needs sustained verified work to reach even median share, paying compute and time per identity while the vine of history keeps its reputation sunk. Scores also decay unless anchored to a karst-like base of completed jobs, so quick cloning yields negligible routing weight and faucet access.
